findings.reason: the plan must add population 2 to the lifecycle exclusion (and plant a never-bound name in the fixture), or state explicitly that never-bound names are retired rather than restored and withdraw them from §38's repair scope and the export's refusal condition; as written, either the exclusion, §38, or the export arm has to change before a node can build §37 as one coherent thing.
findings.text: §37's lifecycle consumer says the orphan lifecycle "excludes from retirement every name the function places in the dropped-edge or unchained-holder population", but §35's census (five populations, at `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-source-loss-census.html`) counts 30 never-bound names, 20 of them at `exhausted`; a never-bound name recorded no source, so it carries no incoming `PRODUCED_NAME`, is non-derived, and is `exhausted` — it matches `supersede_exhausted_standard_name_orphans`' predicate (:22779) exactly and is admitted for retirement. The same paragraph's export arm refuses the release on "any dropped or never-bound live name", and the census states "never-bound names require DD search before retirement", while §38 is written to "Restore each dropped or never-bound source §35 lists" through §36's writers. So the exclusion set contradicts the plan's own cited evidence and the section that depends on it: a node implementing §37 as written leaves 20 exhausted never-bound names to be retired ahead of §38, which then has no live name to search. The fixture mirrors the gap — it plants no never-bound name, so no arm can catch it.
